docs/guide/audio.md:544:- **Nests hear their tracks.** A clip inside a nest plays through its own track inside the nest and through the track the nest clip sits on. Nesting a selection from one track keeps its sound: the nest's copy of that track starts at 0 dB and centre, because the track the nest clip lands on still applies. Clips from the selection's other tracks keep their own track's volume and pan inside the nest, and also get the destination track's. Un-nesting puts the clips back on the timeline's tracks without the nest's track settings. If a nest clip has **Mix to mono** on, pans of the tracks inside it no longer apply.
docs/guide/audio.md:570:- **A nest's bus.** A nest's whole mix plays through the track its nest clip sits on, so a compressor or limiter on that track acts on everything inside the nest together, like a bus. A nest's own tracks have no compressor or limiter: inside an open nest both sections are greyed out, and their tooltip says "A nest's mix plays through the dynamics of the track that holds it." Nesting a selection doesn't copy them; the track the nest clip lands on keeps its own.

21	
22	The window's subtitle tells you where you stand. It reads, for example, `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps · edited` while there are changes that haven't been written, and the word `edited` goes when they have. It's the only sign of unsaved changes, and the close button shows no dot.

42	
43	"edited" clears after <kbd>⌘S</kbd> and after every silent autosave. It's the only sign of unsaved changes: projects autosave in place, so the close button shows no dot. See [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/).

585	- **It's always on.** To silence it, mute or solo tracks, or turn down the Mac's volume.
586	- **Only a scrub on the ruler is heard.** Stepping with ← and →, clicking a marker in the Document tab's Markers list and an agent's `set_playhead` move the playhead silently.

## Format default

The default row. Frame Job works the rate out from the frame's size and rate:

| Format | At 1080p, 30 fps | Bits per pixel per frame |
docs/guide/audio.md:544:- **Nests hear their tracks.** A clip inside a nest plays through its own track inside the nest and through the track the nest clip sits on. Nesting a selection from one track keeps its sound: the nest's copy of that track starts at 0 dB and centre, because the track the nest clip lands on still applies. Clips from the selection's other tracks keep their own track's volume and pan inside the nest, and also get the destination track's. Un-nesting puts the clips back on the timeline's tracks without the nest's track settings. If a nest clip has **Mix to mono** on, pans of the tracks inside it no longer apply.
docs/guide/audio.md:570:- **A nest's bus.** A nest's whole mix plays through the track its nest clip sits on, so a compressor or limiter on that track acts on everything inside the nest together, like a bus. A nest's own tracks have no compressor or limiter: inside an open nest both sections are greyed out, and their tooltip says "A nest's mix plays through the dynamics of the track that holds it." Nesting a selection doesn't copy them; the track the nest clip lands on keeps its own.

input.title: Source comments misstate seven behaviours (default bitrate, wheel alignment, updater, Verify, marker click, dirty indicator, popup right-click)
input.reasoning:
I tried to refute each of the seven items. All seven hold, though [18], [23] and [32] are small overstatements rather than plain errors. No app behaviour is wrong in any of them; only the comments are, and in two cases the site repeated a comment's claim.

[10] Real. export_table.rs:95 says VideoToolbox derives the rate on the writer path. ExporterWriter+Settings.swift:332 always supplies `settings.videoBitrate ?? defaultVideoBitrate(...)`, and its doc comment at about :281 says why VideoToolbox's own default is avoided.

[18] Real but tiny. The arithmetic, using ScopeTraces.chroma's matrices and hueRotation 103, gives a worst offset of 11.76 degrees on Rec. 709, so the comment holds there. On BT.2020, which ScopeTraces uses in HLG, yellow and blue are 12.40 degrees off, so "within 12 degrees" is false in an HLG project. The rotation doesn't change with the project.

[23] Real as an absolute claim. The default is safe: SUAutomaticallyUpdate is unset, so Sparkle does ask. But SUAllowsAutomaticUpdates is also unset, so SUUpdatePermissionPrompt.m:94 and SUUpdateAlert.m:385 show the "Automatically download and install updates" box, and a person who ticks it gets installs with no per-update question. PUB-9 only says Sparkle's defaults apply, so it doesn't make the comment deliberate. Its README index row ("no automatic install") has the same looseness.

[24] Real. effectiveCredential puts the field first. Every real run goes through AssemblyAIConfiguration.credential, which reads the store then the environment. Nothing saves the field except saveClicked, so a typed key is never what a run would use.

[32] Real but imprecise. A click on a timeline marker flag starts a MarkerDragSession or a rename, and mouse-up ends "Move Marker" with no seek (TimelineView.swift:601-609, :787). The only click that seeks is the Go button in the Document tab, plus the menu items. The guide had inherited the loose wording.

[33] Real, and this was the part the report hadn't confirmed. A probe built as ProjectDocument and EditorWindowController are (autosavesInPlace true, same style mask, subtitle set, no toolbar) had window.isDocumentEdited false, so that half of the comment is true. But the title bar gained an NSTextField "—" and an NSButtonTextField "Edited" once the document changed, both untitled and saved. ProjectDocument and EditorWindow override nothing that would suppress this, since the only related overrides are updateChangeCount, which calls super. I did not see it in Frame Job itself, because the task forbids launching it.

[47] Real. OptionPopupControl has no menu and no right-click handling, and inspectorRow puts it directly in InspectorRowView. A stand-in right-clicked through NSWindow.sendEvent reached row.menu(for:). The field half of the comment holds: the same probe opened the text menu for a field at rest and focused.

None of this is recorded as deliberate in the spec, the ADRs or manual-checks, and no open issue matches. Closed #344 was an earlier sweep of comment drift and doesn't cover these.
